name: Grover search (statevector)
summary: Simulate Grover's search on up to 20 qubits and get the exact success probability plus seeded measurement counts.
description:
Runs Grover's quantum search algorithm as a statevector simulation on your machine. You choose the register size and the marked basis states; the product prepares the uniform superposition, applies the phase oracle and the diffusion operator the requested number of times (by default the textbook optimum floor(pi/4 * sqrt(N/M))), and reads the Born-rule distribution off the final state vector.

It is for students checking the amplitude-amplification picture against a real simulation, and for researchers who want an exact, reproducible baseline (success probability from the state vector, plus seeded shot counts) to compare other implementations against.

This is not the older `grover-search` runner family in this SDK, which samples shots from the analytic success probability without simulating a circuit.
useCases: Check the success probability of Grover search for a given number of qubits, marked states and iterations
Show over-rotation: how the success probability falls when iterating past the optimum
Produce a reproducible reference distribution to compare another simulator or SDK against

inputs.name: n_qubits
inputs.description: Register size n; the search space has N = 2^n states. Larger requests are refused with the memory they would need.

inputs.name: marked
inputs.description: Marked basis states as integers in [0, 2^n - 1]; at least one, all distinct, fewer than 2^n.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: Number of Grover iterations k. null uses floor(pi/4 * sqrt(N/M)).

inputs.name: shots
inputs.description: Measurement samples drawn from the final state.

outputs.name: success_probability
outputs.description: Sum of |amplitude|^2 over the marked states of the simulated final state vector (exact up to floating point).

outputs.name: analytic_success_probability
outputs.description: sin^2((2k+1) theta) with sin(theta) = sqrt(M/N), reported beside the simulated value as a cross-check.

outputs.name: iterations
outputs.description: Iterations actually applied, and iterations_rule saying whether they were chosen by the user or by the formula.

outputs.name: counts
outputs.description: Seeded measurement counts, bitstring (most significant qubit first) to count; only non-zero outcomes.

outputs.name: observed_success_fraction
outputs.description: Fraction of shots that landed on a marked state.

changes: First catalog release: NumPy statevector Grover search with exact success probability and seeded sampling.

environment.resources: n=20 with the optimal 804 iterations: ~1.5 s and ~50 MB on a 2024 laptop; time grows as sqrt(N) iterations x N amplitudes.

example.code:
import json
from ketqat_runner import catalog

record = catalog.run("grover-search@1.0.0", seed=7, n_qubits=5, marked=[3, 17], shots=1000)
result = record.result
print(json.dumps({
    "status": record.status,
    "iterations": result["iterations"],
    "success_probability": round(result["success_probability"], 6),
    "analytic_success_probability": round(result["analytic_success_probability"], 6),
}))

verified.platform: macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit (maintainer run of python/tests/test_catalog_examples.py; not yet run by CI)

sampleResult.summary: 5 qubits, marked states 3 and 17, 3 iterations (the optimum): the simulated success probability is 0.961319, equal to the analytic value; 955 of 1000 seeded shots hit a marked state.

assumptions: Ideal, noiseless gates: no decoherence, gate error or readout error is modelled.
The oracle is a phase oracle that flips the sign of each marked basis state; its cost is not modelled.
The diffusion operator is applied in closed form, 2|s><s| - I, which equals H^n (2|0><0| - I) H^n; a test checks the two agree amplitude by amplitude.
scope: 2 to 20 qubits, any non-empty proper subset of marked states, any iteration count up to 100000.
Exact success probability from the state vector and seeded multinomial sampling of measurement outcomes.
limitations: A statevector simulation: memory and time grow as 2^n, so 20 qubits is the ceiling. It says nothing about running on hardware.
No noise model; real devices will show lower success probabilities.
Gate counts and circuit depth are not reported, because the oracle is applied as an operator rather than compiled into gates.
Sampled counts are reproducible for the same seed with the same NumPy version; NumPy does not guarantee identical random streams across versions.
Tested on macOS and Linux only; Windows is untested.

references.title: A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search
references.venue: Proceedings of the 28th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC '96)

references.title: Quantum Computation and Quantum Information: 10th Anniversary Edition

origin.statement: Grover's algorithm was introduced by Lov K. Grover (1996); the multiple-marked-state analysis follows Boyer, Brassard, Hoyer and Tapp (1998). KetQat wrote this NumPy statevector implementation, its validation tests and this catalog entry. KetQat did not invent the method.

contributors.name: dorakingx
contributors.role: KetQat maintainer: implementation, validation and catalog entry

validation.description: Simulated success probability equals sin^2((2k+1) theta), sin(theta) = sqrt(M/N), to 1e-10 for every n in 2..10, several marked-set sizes M and k from 0 past the optimum.
The closed-form diffusion operator equals the gate construction H^n (2|0><0| - I) H^n on random states.
Requests above 20 qubits are refused with the state-vector memory they would need.
The example code is executed verbatim in a clean virtual environment with only this product's extras installed.
